description:
We are three software developers from 42 Málaga using a modular, first-principles approach:

jvernon (Yuls): SAR Science & GIS. Processes offline Sentinel-1/NISAR data, ensuring scientific provenance.

frpozo-l (Fran): Geospatial Backend. Bridges data and UI via a strict data contract, validation, and fast caching.

fradiaz (Javier): Frontend & UX. Transforms complex data into an accessible Streamlit & PyDeck app with reactive charts.
summary:
An interactive SAR subsidence explorer
High-Level Summary: A modular web app that lets anyone scrub through time, watch cities sink, and understand that subsidence is driven by interbed compressibility, not just water pumping.
details:
The Problem: Urban subsidence is a silent crisis. While Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) provides millimeter-accurate displacement data, the sheer size and complexity of HDF5 files create a massive barrier to entry. Furthermore, subsidence is often misunderstood: public perception links it solely to the volume of water pumped, ignoring the critical role of geological interbed compressibility.

Our Solution: "Three Cities, One Pump" is an interactive geospatial explorer that makes SAR data instantly accessible. We built a highly modular system divided into a heavy offline scientific pipeline and a lightweight Streamlit web application.

Our thesis is made visible through a crucial product decision: a shared, symmetric color scale across three case studies.

Mexico City (Inelastic): Shows extreme subsidence (−45 cm/yr) due to its lacustrine clay.

Jakarta (Mixed): Displays severe coastal sinking.

Málaga (Elastic): Acts as our negative control. By rendering nearly flat on the same scale, it proves that despite heavy pumping in confined karst, the geological composition prevents catastrophic subsidence.

Features: Users can scrub through 62 dates on a time slider, filter by coherence or land use, and interrogate individual H3 cells to see displacement series and trends. We prioritize scientific honesty: every layer dynamically displays its source, unit, and exact provenance.

Use of Space Agency Data

Our architecture relies on an offline Python pipeline designed to ingest and process heavy SAR datasets into a versioned, 15 MB data contract (Parquet/JSON).

NISAR (NASA/ISRO): Our pipeline is built to query the ASF DAAC Search API and process NISAR L2 GUNW products. We handle phase/coherence extraction and LOS-to-vertical conversion.

Sentinel-1 (ESA/Copernicus): We use Sentinel-1 C-band data (via HyP3/OPERA DISP-S1) as a robust fallback for historical depth and 6-day revisit intervals.

Copernicus EGMS: Used for cross-validation in our European control case (Málaga).
